study type: Single-center, block-randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind superiority trial
exposure: prophylactic administration of 1 g of intravenous calcium chloride after cord clamping
Patients with and without nonatonic bleeding
1g intravenous calcium chloride after cord clamping
Calcium chloride group vs. placebo group
outcome: Quantitative blood loss at cesarean delivery
cohort: 120 parturients at 34 or more weeks of gestation requiring intrapartum cesarean delivery after oxytocin exposure in labor.
finding: While prophylactic intravenous calcium chloride administration during intrapartum cesarean delivery did not significantly reduce blood loss overall, it did significantly reduce blood loss in a planned subgroup analysis excluding nonatonic bleeding.
